title: Trade-history/ledger table + realized-loss-aware 6% Rule
description: The book's actual 6% Rule formula has two parts: realized losses for the current month PLUS risk on currently open trades. `total_open_risk_pct` (backend/app/portfolio/risk.py) only ever implements the second part -- there is no trade-history/ledger model in the schema at all (app/db/models.py has PositionORM/AccountORM/WatchlistItemORM/OHLCVCacheORM, nothing recording a closed position's realized P&L or close date). Concretely: a user who took three straight stopped-out losses earlier this month, then opens a new, individually-fine 2%-sized position, sails right past the 6% Rule today. Add a closed-trade table (ticker, entry/exit price+date, quantity, realized P&L, and an exit-reason tag per Elder's own taxonomy -- target hit / stop hit / reached value zone / going nowhere / starting to turn / couldn't stand the pain / recognized junk trade after entry), populate it when a position closes, and extend the 6% Rule computation to sum this-month's realized losses alongside open-position risk. This table is also the prerequisite for backend-trade-grading and the trade journal frontend task -- design its schema with those in mind even though implementing them is out of scope here.

checklist.step: Design and add the closed-trade ORM table (ticker, quantity, entry/exit price+date, realized P&L, exit-reason tag) to backend/app/db/models.py, with a migration.
Hook position-close (find/confirm the existing delete-position code path in backend/app/api/routers/portfolio.py) to record a closed-trade row instead of just deleting state.

Extend the 6% Rule computation (a new function alongside total_open_risk_pct, or an extension of it -- decide and record) to sum this calendar month's realized losses from the new table plus existing open-position risk.
Unit tests covering: a month with prior realized losses that pushes a new, individually-fine position over the 6% threshold; a fresh calendar month correctly excluding the prior month's losses.
Regenerate backend/openapi.json/frontend types if any response shape changed; document in docs/Analyse.md §7.

decisions.decision: exit_reason is a Python StrEnum (app.portfolio.models.ExitReason) with Elder's 7 taxonomy tags (target_hit, stop_hit, reached_value_zone, going_nowhere, starting_to_turn, couldnt_stand_the_pain, recognized_junk_trade_after_entry) plus an 8th app-only value, 'unspecified', used as the default. Stored on ClosedTradeORM as a plain String column (no DB-level enum/CHECK constraint), mirroring OHLCVCacheORM.interval's existing 'plain string, Python-layer validation only' convention -- SQLite has no native enum type to enforce it at the DB layer regardless.
decisions.rationale: Elder's own taxonomy has no catch-all category, but DELETE /api/portfolio/positions/{id} has no reliable way to infer why the user is closing a position (no target-price/stop-order concept is tracked anywhere in this app), so an explicit-but-optional query param with a non-Elder default was needed. Rejected: making exit_reason required on DELETE (would break/complicate the existing delete UX for a field the frontend doesn't collect yet -- that's the trade-journal task's job); inferring a reason algorithmically from price-vs-stop/price-vs-channel (would require fetching/recomputing protective_stop and the Autoenvelope band inside what's otherwise a simple DB delete, adding a data-provider dependency risk to an endpoint that must keep working even when a position's price/history can't be fetched).

decisions.decision: DELETE /api/portfolio/positions/{id} prices the closed_trades row's exit_price from today's latest close via the same market-data lookup GET /api/portfolio and GET /api/portfolio/risk already use for current_price (app.portfolio.pricing.latest_close, promoted from a private _latest_close to a public function since it now has two callers) -- not a caller-supplied exit_price. If that fetch fails (unknown/delisted ticker, provider unavailable), the position is still deleted, but no closed_trades row is recorded.
decisions.rationale: This app already treats 'current market price' as the authoritative mark-to-market source everywhere else (never a client-supplied number), so pricing the exit the same way is consistent rather than introducing a second, inconsistent pricing path. A data-provider outage must never block removing a position (deleting is the one operation that should always succeed, since a stuck position blocks nothing else the user might want to do), and a closed trade with no real exit price would poison realized_pnl (and so the 6% Rule) with a fabricated number -- silently skipping the closed_trades row is preferable to inventing a price or failing the whole DELETE.

decisions.decision: The 6% Rule's realized-losses-this-month component is a new sibling function, app.portfolio.risk.realized_losses_pct(account, realized_losses_this_month), not a single combined function alongside/replacing total_open_risk_pct. The calendar-month closed_trades DB query itself lives in a new router-level helper, app.api.routers.portfolio._realized_losses_this_month_pct, which sums both via simple addition at the GET /api/portfolio/risk call site. The RiskResponse field keeps its existing name total_open_risk_pct for the combined total (its description is updated to explain both halves), plus a new realized_losses_this_month_pct field exposing the realized-losses half on its own for transparency/debuggability.
decisions.rationale: app.portfolio.risk has no DB dependency anywhere else (Account/Position are plain domain models, not ORM rows) -- a single combined function would have to either take an already-summed dollar figure (making it barely different from two sibling functions summed by the caller) or import SQLAlchemy/ClosedTradeORM itself (breaking that module boundary for one caller). Keeping total_open_risk_pct's own behavior/tests untouched (it still means exactly what its existing unit tests already assert) avoids rewriting a well-covered, already-shipped function's contract. Renaming the RiskResponse field instead of keeping total_open_risk_pct was considered and rejected: it is the field this response has always compared against the 6% threshold and existing frontend code (RiskPanel.tsx, RiskSummaryCard.tsx) already reads it under this name -- broadening its documented meaning costs less than a rename that would ripple through the frontend for no behavioral gain.

decisions.decision: Closing a position via DELETE does not adjust AccountORM.cash (no automatic credit of sale proceeds back to the cash balance).
decisions.rationale: Matches the existing, already-shipped precedent: POST /api/portfolio/positions (buying/adding a position) likewise never debits cash. Cash is entirely user-managed (docs/Analyse.md §9: 'cash balance entered or imported by the user'), and introducing automatic cash bookkeeping on the sell side only, while the buy side stays manual, would be an inconsistent half-measure -- a full auto-cash-sync feature (if ever wanted) belongs in its own task covering both sides.

decisions.decision: Did not update the frontend's 'Total Open Risk' StatCard label/copy (RiskPanel.tsx, RiskSummaryCard.tsx) to reflect that the underlying field now also includes this month's realized losses, beyond the minimal fixture changes needed to keep tsc/tests passing against the widened RiskResponse type.
decisions.rationale: This task is scoped backend/db (skill add-api-endpoint, no add-frontend-feature); a genuine label/copy change would ripple across both risk components, their unit tests, PortfolioPage.test.tsx, DashboardPage.test.tsx, two Storybook stories, and two Playwright e2e specs -- real UI-facing feature work, not a type-compatibility fix, and better scoped to the already-planned frontend-trade-journal task (or its own follow-up) where the realized-losses breakdown can be surfaced properly (e.g. showing the two components separately) rather than a quick label edit here.

comments.summary: New tests in test_portfolio_delete_position.py (test_records_closed_trade_with_default_unspecified_exit_reason) and test_portfolio_risk.py (TestRealizedLossesThisMonth) assert against local date.today()-derived fixtures/expectations, but the production code that sets/reads the same dates (app.api.routers.portfolio._today()) is explicitly UTC-based, matching every other 'now' helper in this codebase. Harmless today (dev container/CI both run in UTC) but a latent flake source outside UTC, and near a month boundary could put a fixture's ClosedTradeORM row in the wrong bucket relative to what the UTC-based query actually uses. Non-blocking; tracked as a follow-up.

RiskSummaryCard.tsx/RiskPanel.tsx's 'Total Open Risk' label now silently covers a combined open-risk + this-month's-realized-losses figure with no copy change -- a deliberate, well-reasoned deferral per this task's own decisions entry (backend-scoped task; real copy/breakdown work better paired with the future trade-journal frontend task). Confirmed a corresponding decisions entry exists per CLAUDE.md's cross-check requirement. Non-blocking; tracked as a follow-up so the deferred UI work isn't forgotten.

frontend/src/pages/DashboardPage.test.tsx and PortfolioPage.test.tsx build RiskResponse MSW fixtures that were not updated to include the new required realized_losses_this_month_pct field, unlike every other RiskResponse fixture touched in this PR. Currently harmless (untyped mock, field unread by any component under test) but an inconsistency within this PR's own diff. Non-blocking; tracked as a follow-up.

review.notes:
Full review of PR #148 (branch task/backend-trade-history-table, already checked out at dispatch). Backend: source backend/.venv/bin/activate && python -m pytest --cov=app --cov-branch --cov-report=term-missing -> 615 passed, 99.89% coverage (matches PR claim), gate 90% met. Frontend: yarn test --run -> 349 passed; yarn test --coverage --run -> 99.69% statements/99.44% branches (matches PR claim). Static analysis (static-verify skill): backend ruff clean, mypy clean (40 files); frontend eslint clean, tsc -b --noEmit clean. openapi.json regenerated via scripts/export_openapi.py and diffed against the committed snapshot -- no diff, genuinely in sync. docs/Analyse.md §6% Rule and docs/architecture/API.md both accurately describe the new two-part formula and DELETE's new exit_reason param/closed_trades recording; cross-checked against docs/ideas.md's ch. 51 note, which this PR's own decisions/description correctly cite.

Methodology correctness (verify-elder-signal-style scrutiny, area=backend/portfolio): read app.portfolio.risk.realized_losses_pct and app.api.routers.portfolio._realized_losses_this_month_pct/get_risk/delete_position in full. Confirmed the 6% Rule genuinely sums this-calendar-month realized losses (only losing trades, exit_date in [month_start, as_of]) plus open-position risk (total_open_risk_pct over positions with a known stop) at the GET /api/portfolio/risk call site, matching Elder ch. 51's two-part formula. Month-boundary handling verified by reading the actual filter (ClosedTradeORM.exit_date >= as_of.replace(day=1) AND <= as_of), not just trusting test names -- test_fresh_calendar_month_excludes_prior_months_realized_losses and test_prior_realized_losses_this_month_push_an_individually_fine_position_over_six_percent both construct fixtures with an explicit last-day-of-prior-month vs. this-month date and assert the correct inclusion/exclusion. No double counting: a deleted position is removed from PositionORM (so excluded from the open-risk half on the next GET /portfolio or /risk call) in the same transaction its closed_trades row is inserted, and test_a_realized_loss_from_delete_shows_up_in_get_risk_immediately plus test_deleted_position_no_longer_appears_in_get_portfolio both cover this directly. Exit-price sourcing (app.portfolio.pricing.latest_close, promoted from private, same close-only-NaN-checked lookup current_price already uses) degrades to skipping the closed_trades row entirely (not a zero/fabricated price) on fetch failure -- test_position_still_deleted_when_price_fetch_fails_but_no_closed_trade_recorded confirms no row is written rather than a wrong realized_pnl silently entering the 6% Rule.

Migration (2e81d22e2f96_add_closed_trades_table.py): create_table/two indexes in upgrade, symmetric drop_index x2 + drop_table in downgrade -- correct and reversible; covered by test_db_migrations.py's extended upgrade/downgrade round-trip. DELETE endpoint behavior change: response is still 204 No Content on the same path/shape as before (verified both via the integration suite and a live e2e run -- see below), so no existing consumer/test expectation broke; new behavior (closed_trades recording, optional exit_reason query param defaulting to unspecified) is additive. exit_reason=<invalid> correctly 422s (schema-level enum validation via FastAPI Query(...)).

Decision cross-check (CLAUDE.md): all 3 checklist items phrased as a judgment call ('decide and record' on the risk-computation shape; the exit-reason enum representation/default; the exit-price sourcing) have corresponding decisions entries with real rationale (not bare 'changed X'), plus two more decisions (no auto cash-adjustment on close, frontend label left untouched) -- 5 total, all substantive.

UI-facing work (step 9/9a): this PR changes DELETE /api/portfolio/positions/{id} (consumed by the existing delete-position button/dialog in PortfolioPage) and RiskResponse's total_open_risk_pct value (consumed by RiskPanel/RiskSummaryCard/Dashboard), so a browser walkthrough applies. No Playwright MCP tools were available in this session; drove the app instead with a real Chromium browser via the frontend's own installed playwright package (frontend/node_modules/.bin/playwright), started via `make backend`/`make frontend`. Golden path: loaded /portfolio, deleted AKBA (a losing position) via the UI confirm dialog, verified via direct API calls that the position was removed from GET /api/portfolio and a realized loss appeared in GET /api/portfolio/risk's realized_losses_this_month_pct; deleted MSFT next and, waiting long enough for the UI to settle (~3s), confirmed the positions table, StatCards, and risk panel all correctly reflected the removal with no console errors and no failed network requests (aside from a benign Chromium artifact where a 204 No Content DELETE response is also reported via requestfailed/net::ERR_ABORTED -- confirmed via response-status logging that the request actually succeeded with 204; a pre-existing browser/CDP quirk unrelated to this PR's change, not a real regression). Edge case: observed that after deleting 3 positions without any cash credit (an already-existing, explicitly-decided design choice -- decisions entry 'no automatic cash-balance adjustment on position close'), total_open_risk_pct/realized_losses_this_month_pct balloon to very large percentages (e.g. 572%) because the shrinking equity denominator now also divides the realized-losses numerator this PR adds -- mechanically correct given the already-accepted no-cash-credit design, not a bug introduced by this PR, but flagged in the follow-up task since this PR is what makes the effect materially worse than before (previously only open-position risk divided by the same shrinking equity).

Also ran the persisted e2e suite (step 9a, e2e-test skill): `make e2e` -> 16/16 specs passed across dashboard/navigation/portfolio/stock-analysis/watchlist, including portfolio.spec.ts's own add/view/delete-position flow (DELETE ... 204 No Content, position removed from the table) -- no regression from this PR's DELETE/risk changes.

pr_decision.notes: Independently re-ran backend (615 passed, 99.89% cov) and frontend (349 passed) suites plus tsc -b --noEmit (clean) and openapi.json regeneration (no diff) -- all match pr-reviewer's claims. Read the full diff (git diff main...task/backend-trade-history-table): confirmed the 6% Rule genuinely sums this-calendar-month realized losses (app.portfolio.risk.realized_losses_pct + app.api.routers.portfolio._realized_losses_this_month_pct's exit_date filter, month_start<=exit_date<=as_of) plus open-position risk at the GET /api/portfolio/risk call site; hand-verified TestRealizedLossesThisMonth's reference value myself (6600.0 realized losses / 100103.0 equity * 100 = 6.593%, matches the test's assertion and exceeds the 6% threshold as claimed); confirmed month-boundary exclusion test uses last-day-of-prior-month dates correctly excluded by the >= month_start filter; confirmed no double-counting -- delete_position's db.add(ClosedTradeORM(...)) and db.delete(row) share a single db.commit(), so a deleted position and its closed-trade record are never both visible mid-transaction; confirmed the migration's downgrade (drop_index x2 + drop_table) symmetrically reverses upgrade's create_table + create_index x2. Verified the 3 filed non-blocking findings are accurate and genuinely non-blocking (date.today() vs UTC _today() mismatch in new tests is real but harmless in UTC CI; the two flagged frontend test files build untyped risk fixtures, confirmed via grep no RiskResponse type is imported there, and tsc stayed clean). No new issues found; accept holds.
